children.label: a
children.prompt: Describe what happens to $y$ as $x\to\infty$ and as $x\to-\infty$ for $y=x^2(x-4)^2$.

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}y&=x^2(x-4)^2\\&\text{leading term }x^4\\&\text{even power, positive coefficient}\\&\text{so }y\to\infty\text{ as }x\to\infty\text{ and as }x\to-\infty\end{align*}$$

answer.short: The graph crosses the $x$-axis at $x=2$ with a horizontal tangent (a flat crossing).
answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}y&=x(x-2)^3\\&(x-2)\text{ is a triple factor}\\&\text{so at }x=2\text{ the graph crosses the }x\text{-axis, flattening out horizontally as it passes through}\end{align*}$$
